incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — ransomware (plus a second unattributed intruder)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of on-premises SharePoint servers followed by abuse of legitimate tools (Velociraptor, Cloudflare tunneling, Zoho Assist, VS Code SSH) for persistence, while a second unrelated actor used DLL sideloading and custom backdoors in parallel.
incidents.impact: Microsoft Incident Response uncovered two distinct threat actors operating simultaneously in one hybrid environment, with privilege escalation, new admin accounts, and defense-evasion via a vulnerable driver; the intrusion was contained and the customer remediated.

incidents.vector: A Rust-based clipboard-hijacking malware spread via a fake WordPress 'tools' site, amplified by an elaborate cross-platform reputation network (GitHub, SourceForge, AI-narrated YouTube videos, and manipulated 'safe' votes on VirusTotal).
incidents.impact: Check Point detailed a global crypto-theft campaign that swaps wallet addresses on the clipboard to redirect Bitcoin, Ethereum, Monero, Binance Chain, and Solana transactions; notable for manipulating reputation systems to defeat trust- and reputation-based detection.

incidents.vector: Mass credential attempts (~1.16B against FortiGate, ~2.1B against MSSQL) plus interception of SSL VPN authentication hashes cracked offline on a 45-GPU cluster, likely sourced from exported FortiGate configuration files.
incidents.impact: The 'FortiBleed' dataset exposed valid admin and SSL VPN credentials for 73,932 firewalls across 21,600+ domains; researchers verified samples as authentic, many devices remain online, and a Turkish NATO defense contractor allegedly had classified documents exfiltrated.

incidents.vector: Ransomware intrusion claimed by the 'Gentlemen' ransomware-as-a-service group using double extortion; the company confirmed an external party accessed parts of its IT environment.
incidents.impact: Australia's second-largest sugar producer had its Racecourse and Farleigh mills shut since June 10, halting harvesting across much of Queensland's Mackay cane region at the start of crushing season; the group threatens to leak allegedly stolen data.

incidents.vector: Compromised LiteLLM package versions (1.82.7, 1.82.8) published to PyPI — likely via a hijacked maintainer account — containing code to steal cloud credentials, API keys, and crypto wallets and install a persistent downloader.
incidents.impact: An open-source AI package with ~3M daily downloads, present in roughly 36% of cloud environments, was poisoned for at least two hours; researchers warn tens of thousands of corporate environments may be affected, with downstream credential-reuse risk. Part of a broader campaign claimed by TeamPCP.

incidents.vector: Initial access via the Trivy supply-chain compromise (attributed to TeamPCP), then misuse of a secret Amazon API key to access the Commission's AWS-hosted Europa.eu platform.
incidents.impact: CERT-EU attributed a March 19 breach in which ~92GB of compressed data — names, email addresses, and some email content affecting 42 internal clients and 29+ EU entities — was taken and later posted on ShinyHunters' leak site on March 28.

incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — credential theft (Mini Shai-Hulud worm variant)
incidents.vector: A compromised GitHub account pushed a 'Miasma' variant of the self-propagating Mini Shai-Hulud worm to distribute credential-stealing malware to developers.
incidents.impact: Red Hat pulled 32 tainted packages (downloaded ~117,000 times weekly) after the compromise; part of a cascading series of supply-chain intrusions stemming from TeamPCP's publicly released worm code, though specific attribution remains uncertain.

incidents.victim: North American medical, academic & military research institutions
incidents.vector: Exploitation of externally facing REDCap research servers, deployment of custom 'INFINITERED' malware to harvest credentials, then pivot to internal networks and abuse of Google Workspace content-compliance rules to covertly BCC-forward emails.
incidents.impact: Google Threat Intelligence detailed a PRC-nexus campaign (active since September 2023, undetected for over a year) targeting research on AI, uncrewed systems, offensive cyber, national defense, and medicine; Google disrupted the infrastructure and notified victims.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to parts of the company's internal network; specifics undisclosed.
incidents.impact: The Danish pharmaceutical giant (maker of Ozempic and Wegovy) took systems offline to investigate and evict attackers, confirming some sensitive data including patient PII was copied during the intrusion.

incidents.vector: Compromise of a developer laptop and theft of private multisig keys.
incidents.impact: Attackers stole roughly $36 million in crypto-assets; the Humanity token lost nearly 90% of its value shortly after the heist.

incidents.vector: Attackers abused the AUR 'adopt orphaned package' mechanism to take over abandoned packages and add installation steps pulling a malicious npm package (later swapped to a Bun script) that installed a rootkit and infostealer.
incidents.impact: More than 1,900 community AUR packages were hijacked over a weekend to deploy a rootkit and a credential/secrets harvester targeting browsers, Electron apps, and developer keys; hijack attempts were still ongoing at the time of reporting.

incidents.vector: Malicious code added to legitimate JavaScript files of three plugins (OptinMonster, TrustPulse, PushEngage) that waits for an admin login, creates a rogue admin account, and installs a self-hiding backdoor plugin.
incidents.impact: More than 1.2 million websites were backdoored following a security incident at the major WordPress plugin developer Awesome Motive.

incidents.vector: Data theft from an unsecured database exposed online, claimed by the FulcrumSec group.
incidents.impact: Terabytes of data were stolen from the K-12 operator (12 brands, 65 campuses) — including passport details of children and parents, attendance records, teacher passwords, and visitor photos — and leaked after ransom negotiations failed.

incidents.victim: Major Iranian banks (Bank Melli, Tejarat, Saderat, Export Development Bank)
incidents.vector: Attack reportedly targeting shared communications infrastructure used by the four banks.
incidents.impact: Online portals and mobile apps for four of Iran's largest banks were down over a weekend; the country's banking council said no customer data was accessed.

incidents.vector: Data theft from a third-party supplier (TINYpulse), claimed by the Shadowbyt3$ data-extortion group.
incidents.impact: Hackers are seeking a $2 million ransom, claiming nearly 1GB of employee and business data stolen via the supplier; not yet confirmed by Nintendo.

incidents.vector: Alleged breach of a government agency managing healthcare entitlements; specifics undisclosed.
incidents.impact: Hackers claim to have stolen the personal information of more than 67 million Thai citizens, some of which was posted on online black markets; the government has launched a probe.

incidents.vector: Compromise of the lawmaker's Signal messaging account; method undisclosed.
incidents.impact: The FBI notified Rep. Bacon — a vocal Ukraine supporter and Kremlin critic — that suspected Russian hackers breached his Signal account.

incidents.victim: Higher education sector (incl. University of Nottingham, Council of Europe)
incidents.vector: Zero-day exploitation of Oracle PeopleSoft (CVE-2026-35273, CVSS 9.8) targeting Environment Management Hub endpoints, followed by MeshCentral agents masquerading as Azure services, SSH credential spraying, and a defacement/extortion fan-out script.
incidents.impact: Mandiant/GTIG notified 100+ exposed organizations (68% higher education); compromised data was published on ShinyHunters' leak site. Related victims include the University of Nottingham (40GB, 450,000+ students/alumni) and the Council of Europe (297GB claimed).

incidents.vector: At least 13 fake 'consulting company' websites with AI-generated photos and personas, advertised via hiring platforms, used to recruit current and former clearance holders and pressure them for insider information in exchange for payment.
incidents.impact: DOJ and FBI seized 13 domains used by suspected Chinese agents (active since November 2023) to lure clearance holders into disclosing classified or sensitive U.S. government information; takedown pages were placed to disrupt the scheme.

incidents.vector: Abuse of an API bug to access data from ServiceNow customer instances; reportedly exploited since at least April.
incidents.impact: ServiceNow quietly patched the platform and notified affected customers, with incidents mainly impacting its Australia platform release.

incidents.vector: A spear-phishing operation luring WhatsApp users into clicking malicious links leading to an external site.
incidents.impact: Meta says it disrupted a new NSO Group campaign targeting WhatsApp users in violation of a U.S. court injunction, and filed to hold NSO in contempt; it urged lawmakers to keep NSO's sanctions in place.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to the university's CareerConnect careers platform in late May.
incidents.impact: Attackers stole data on alumni, research staff, and employers from the platform Oxford uses to connect students and staff with recruiters.
